reason: The contract (problem.txt, the operative artifact since no test.py/get_inputs exist) requires the unnormalized forward real DFT per row with per-component tolerance abs(actual-exact) <= 1e-4 + 1e-6*abs(exact) for every legal input (B 1..256, N in {64,128,256}, all finite FP16 values). Confirmed in-scope claim c1 shows via runtime probe t8 that run() executes without exception on all N in {64,128,256} and B in {1,7,256} using ordinary random FP16 inputs, but nearly every non-DC bin violates the tolerance: max error/tolerance ratio ~1.2e5-4.9e5 (e.g. N256_B256: 65024 of 66048 components violate, max_err 65.03). This is a structural correctness failure (misindexed gather/permutation path on Triton 3.4.0), not a rounding artifact — the deviation is orders of magnitude beyond any tolerance the contract allows. Confirmed claim c2 corroborates the same failure at legal extreme-magnitude inputs (all +/-65504 rows at N=256, ratio ~1.25e8). No contract clause (rounding, reduction order, layout) can account for errors of this magnitude; input storage was preserved and outputs were finite, so the failure is purely numerical correctness. Both claims have scope evidence citing the stated input domain from problem.txt, all open claims have evidence, and the Skeptic recorded no new claims after reviewing this evidence. Verdict: reject.
